scope: Owner-approved installation key, signed connection, sequenced text and foreground visibility in the shared Cosmos/Center room, with one shared-room visual card acknowledged after the installation's exact render and one shared-room spoken reply synthesized by Cosmos under the origin's speech-provider disclosure, streamed as bounded frames and acknowledged after the installation's complete playback. Native capture and physical device acceptance remain unfinished.
legacyProfile: native-shared-display-v2 approvals keep rendering cards and connecting but play no speech until the owner reapproves at the current revision.

fields.publicKey: canonical unpadded base64url of a valid 65-byte uncompressed SEC1 P-256 point

owner.errorScope: Cosmos owner routes below. The Center BFF preserves status but sanitizes codes; its same-origin check can also return 403.
owner.authentication: Verified owner bearer; Center uses authenticated same-origin BFF. Native possession never substitutes for owner approval.

routes.POST /surface-api/v1/native: descriptor plus required expectedRevision; response {native: NativeSurface}
routes.GET /surface-api/v1/native/enrollments/:: Owner-scoped lookup including revoked records; response {native: NativeSurface}

owner.revision: Create uses expectedRevision 0. Reapproval/revocation uses the current approval revision. Exact active approval retry preserves revision. Liveness does not change approval revision.
owner.locator: Enrollment locators are globally unique and cannot transfer owners, including after revocation. Descriptor/key/platform are immutable; a different key requires a new enrollment locator.
owner.link: Clients may hand the public descriptor to Center as the fragment `#descriptor=<unpadded base64url JSON>` on /settings/account/surfaces, typed, opened or scanned from a QR code. Center consumes the fragment locally, validates it exactly like pasted text, clears it from the address bar and still requires the owner's fingerprint comparison and explicit approval; the fragment is never sent to a server.

challenge.publicKeyFingerprint: SHA256 lowercase hex of SEC1 public-key bytes
challenge.nonce: canonical unpadded base64url of 32 random bytes

challenge.audience: Cosmos uses REVIVAL_PUBLIC_ORIGIN, never Host or forwarded headers. Invalid/missing configuration returns 503. The native client must match the received canonical audience against its configured server before signing.
challenge.retry: At most one pending challenge per approved installation. Anonymous repeats return the same unexpired challenge without replacing it or extending expiry. A new challenge does not erase the previous successful open retry result.

request.expectedIncarnation: required non-nil UUID or null, exactly challenge.currentIncarnation
request.sessionTokenHash: SHA256 lowercase hex of fresh locally retained 32-byte session secret
request.signature: canonical unpadded base64url of strict DER ECDSA P-256/SHA256 signature

open.commit: Recheck approval and binding, verify exact pending challenge/signature, enforce incarnation CAS, consume challenge and commit connection plus ledger atomically. Invalid proof does not consume a pending challenge.
open.retry: Idempotency hashes signing-message bytes, not ECDSA signature bytes. An exact consumed retry returns only the same still-current approved connection, with unchanged expiry and lease. Replaced, expired, revoked or reapproved connections reject the old retry. Persist the pending attempt before sending; response loss is not proof of failure.
open.secrets: The private key stays on the client. Room authentication sends the raw session secret only to Cosmos over HTTPS; durable state stores its digest. Owner views and open responses contain neither credential. Fresh connection requires a fresh challenge and fresh session secret.

room.authentication: Exactly one Authorization: Bearer header containing canonical unpadded base64url of the raw 32-byte session secret. Hash decoded bytes, never the base64 spelling. The stored digest, its base64 encoding and owner JWTs are not bearer capabilities.

request.approvalRevision: positive safe integer matching current connection
request.epoch: non-nil boot UUID matching current connection

room.response: Same Connection object as contracts/ambiance-room.json: version, url, token, participant, runtimeParticipant, runtimeEpoch and epoch.
room.authority: Resolve principal/surface through the durable enrollment locator. Check current proof, approval revision and epoch before room setup, then recheck in the shared coordinator before and after SFU setup. Room joins and exact retries do not open a replacement connection or renew any deadline.
room.coordination: One shared room manager and runtime participant for Browser and Native. The existing cosmos.coordinate.v1 RPC carries sequenced text and native heartbeat/cancel/state/acknowledge controls. Native participants receive render and clear frames for one card, speak frames for one spoken reply, invite frames while a private card waits for them and status frames for the turns they originate; they receive no media grants.

input.message: {version:1,kind:"input",stamp:{epoch,sequence,instanceId},text:"1-4000 UTF-8 bytes",target?:"browser|macos|linux|android|android_tv",context?:{kind:"screen",app:"1-64 UTF-8 bytes",text:"1-8000 UTF-8 bytes"}}; both optional fields may be omitted, and unknown fields or kinds are rejected.
input.target: The request's own explicit destination. It carries exactly the weight of cognition's target hint (a bounded rank component for eligible non-origin surfaces of that kind), outranks the model's target when both exist, is logged as the decision's hint, and never makes a hidden, blocked or unapproved surface eligible.
input.context: Bounded text from the origin's own screen. It raises the turn's privacy floor to private (the runtime's classifier terms can raise it further; sensitive is refused before cognition) and is bound into the request digest, so an exact retry must replay the same target and context. Only the whole serialized message fits the 12 KiB RPC envelope; over-long input is rejected.
input.retry: An exact retry (same stamp, text, target and context) returns the same admission; the same sequence with a different target or context is refused.

status.recipient: Only the native member that originated the current turn, once per committed state change: working (turn begun), waiting (an action is proposed or dispatched to a surface of the named kind), shown/spoken (that action was acknowledged there), nowhere (nothing was eligible or the turn ended without output), unknown (delivery deadlines exhausted). A terminal state ends the turn's frames; a member that joins later receives the current state once. Browsers receive no status frames.
status.expression: Outcome-gated and reason-free: the frame names the kind of surface, never a surface identity, content or why nothing was eligible. Privacy suppression, capability misses and ordinary re-routing look identical, and privacy is the class the status is expressed at, capped by the origin's own ceiling (shared_room unless the origin is a personal surface), so a private card shown on the phone reports only state shown with surface android.

screenContext.permission: Owner policy at GET/POST /surface-api/v1/surfaces/:surfaceId/screen-context, body {approval:"approve-screen-context-v1",approvalRevision,expectedRevision,policy:{maximumClass:"private"}|null}, response {approval:{approvalRevision,revision,policy}}. Native surfaces only (a Pin or browser is not found); it binds to the installation's approval revision like private-display and is dropped by reapproval or revocation. Ledger event screen_context_policy_changed.
screenContext.flow: A turn with context is private and needs a personal surface declared for that class; without one it is refused before cognition. With the origin's permission at its current revision the runtime records screen_context_offered {fence, appDigest, bytes} (never the text) and hands cognition the text after the user's request as a delimited untrusted block ("=== BEGIN SCREEN CONTEXT ... === END SCREEN CONTEXT ===") that the system prompt names as data, never instructions. Without the permission the runtime proposes a private card explaining that screen context must be allowed for this device in Center and sends the text nowhere.
screenContext.routing: The reply is at least private and follows the private policy: only personal surfaces on their card channel, every shared surface suppressed with a privacy blocker, never speech. Provider lookups derived from a private turn are refused by the existing lookup ceilings.

choices.content: {kind:"choices",title:"1-120 UTF-8 bytes",items:[{id:"1".."8" in order,title:"1-80 UTF-8 bytes",detail:"0-200 UTF-8 bytes"}]} with two to eight items and no control characters; a render frame carries it like text or places, and clients reject anything else.
choices.digest: SHA-256 of the compact JSON of ["cosmos.choice-list",1,title,[[id,title,detail],...]] with items in order, byte-for-byte the runtime's binding.
choices.proposal: Cognition proposes choice_list:{title,items:[{title,detail}]} as its own branch of propose_information (strict XOR with intent, analysis, web_lookup and place_lookup); the runtime numbers the items and rejects any bound violation before the proposal exists.
choices.memory: When a choice list at or below shared_room is acknowledged, the runtime remembers "title: 1. first; 2. second" as recent context of kind choices for ten minutes (ledger recent_context_remembered) and offers the next turn one sentence naming the numbered items, so "play trailer for number two" resolves into a web_lookup for "<title> trailer" or an informational answer. No media playback exists yet; a private list is never remembered.

room.lifecycle: A fresh heartbeat extends only the 45-second lease, capped by the one-hour absolute expiry. Input and controls share one durable high-water cursor. Exact retries do not renew or invoke cognition again. Expired connections cannot revive. Disconnect closes only the exact native connection and its pending turn, preserving owner approval and the same-boot cursor.

privateRouting.permission: Owner policy at GET/POST /surface-api/v1/surfaces/:surfaceId/private-display (approve-private-display-v1, policy {maximumClass: near_user|private} or null) states that one native installation may show private replies while the owner is present and it is unlocked. It binds to the installation's approval revision, is refused for android_tv, and is the owner's statement about the device: Cosmos cannot verify who is looking at the screen. GET /surface-api/v1/native rows carry connected, visible and privateDisplay for the owner's device list.
privateRouting.sameTurn: A request above shared_room from any origin is answered in the same turn: the runtime builds the reply from the owner's saved notes itself, without cognition or any provider (ledger private_context_offered), and proposes it at the request's class. Policy admits only personal installations declared for that class (the visual card channel, never speech); every shared surface is suppressed with a privacy blocker. Sensitive requests and requests with no personal surface for the class are refused before cognition, indistinguishably from a capability miss.
privateRouting.waiting: A personal installation holds the private card while its signed connection is current even when its app is not in front: the card is proposed for it with a five-minute display window and is claimed by Poll only once the installation reports visible from an unlocked foreground. Reporting not visible after dispatch retires the card.
privateRouting.invite: While a private card waits, that member receives {version:1,kind:"invite",stamp,invitation:{version:1,id,surfaceId,incarnation,origin:"pin|browser|macos|linux|android|android_tv",privacy,expiresAt}} once per offer and {invitation:null} when it is dispatched, withdrawn or expired; both take the usual received receipt. The frame never carries content, so a notification built from it may say only that something is ready.
privateRouting.expression: The shared origin expresses nothing that names privacy: a Pin origin receives the same outcome-gated confirmation sentence it receives for any card acknowledged elsewhere, proposed at shared_room as the runtime's own expression (Decision.expression=true) only after the personal installation acknowledged its exact render.
privateRouting.render: Render commands carry privacy. A card above shared_room is shown only on the unlocked personal foreground, never previewed or spoken.

speech.disclosure: Owner policy at GET/POST /surface-api/v1/surfaces/:surfaceId/speech-disclosure (approve-speech-provider-disclosure-v1) permits synthesis of the origin surface's shared reply text through Azure Speech. The policy is keyed by the turn's origin (Pin or native); a native surface is an eligible audio.tts target only with the current speech profile, a visible current connection and a permitting origin policy. Speech with no eligible surface is re-proposed as the same text on a visual card.
speech.dispatch: Poll never stock-claims audio for a room member. The room coordinator starts one synthesis job per member and proposed audio action; StartDisclosure atomically claims the exact action under the origin policy, and the disclosure is rechecked before every provider chunk and on every state change. Failure before any frame leaves the action to expire; failure after a frame records DeliveryFailed; drop retires the exact turn.

frames.chunk: Same bound fields with sequence n+1, chunk (standard base64 of at most 8192 audio bytes) and final on the last frame; no text.
frames.receipt: {version:1,kind:"received",stamp} exactly as for render frames; a receipt is transport evidence only.
frames.format: Azure audio-24khz-48kbitrate-mono-mp3, whole reply at most 1048576 bytes; contentDigest is SHA-256 of the spoken text, byte-for-byte the disclosed synthesis input.
frames.clear: A clear frame naming the action retires the delivered or partial reply; the client stops playback and never acknowledges it.

speech.acknowledgment: The installation plays the exact assembled bytes once and then sends the sequenced acknowledge control with channel audio.tts, the action's turn/generation and contentDigest. Only a current native member may acknowledge audio; an interrupted, replaced or retired reply is never acknowledged.
speech.clients: The shared Rust client assembles frames and exposes the reply with its audio; the C/JNI bindings report speech in snapshots without the bytes and copy the bytes on request. macOS plays through AVAudioPlayer and Android through MediaPlayer; both hold no provider credentials and substitute no operating-system voice.

signing.algorithm: ECDSA P-256 with SHA-256 over the complete transcript bytes exactly once; strict DER signature, maximum 72 bytes.
signing.byteOrder: big-endian; UUIDs are their 16 network-order bytes, never their textual spelling

encodings.utf8-u16be: Unsigned 16-bit byte length followed by UTF-8 bytes, no terminator.
encodings.optional-uuid: One byte 0 for null; otherwise one byte 1 followed by the 16 UUID bytes.
encodings.sha256-hex: Decode exactly 64 lowercase hex characters to 32 bytes.
encodings.base64url-32: Decode canonical unpadded base64url to exactly 32 bytes.

postgresql.scope: Native enrollment locator reads, owner native approval/revocation, native challenge/open/check/close, and native room input/control runtime operations.
postgresql.semantics: Set before table queries and reset at transaction end. These bound each server-side statement/lock wait, not the complete transaction. HTTP timeout can still leave a commit outcome uncertain; recover through the exact pending signed attempt.

limitations: Software key possession is not hardware attestation or speaker identity.
Platform is an owner-reviewed display hint, not a permission or capability proof.
The declared text capability is a fixed approval ceiling. Enrollment alone cannot originate a request; current connection proof and room admission are required. Native output remains ineligible.
Native text and controls use the shared room RPC only. There is no parallel REST input/control/state/close interface, and native participants cannot acknowledge browser rendering.
This wire contract and its vectors do not establish installed clients, production acceptance or paper conformance.

legacyProfile.status: Persisted approvals stay input-only until the owner reapproves at the current revision; reapproval bumps the revision and drops the current connection.

display.eligibility: A native surface is a visual.card candidate only with the current display manifest, a current signed connection and a state control reporting visible=true on that connection. Visibility is availability, never occupancy, privacy or actor evidence.
display.frames: Runtime render/clear frames use the browser room wire shape; the client replies {version:1,kind:"received",stamp} only for a frame naming its exact surface/incarnation with a matching content digest and supported credit grammar.
display.controls: {kind:"state",visible} and {kind:"acknowledge",actionId,turnId,generation,channel:"visual.card",contentDigest} share the native input cursor; acknowledge instance IDs equal the action ID and are accepted only for actions dispatched to that connection.
display.hint: Cognition may propose target browser|macos|linux|android|android_tv from explicit request text. Policy adds a bounded rank component for eligible non-origin surfaces of that kind only; blocked or hidden surfaces and self-nomination gain nothing.
